subject: understanding number of elements in the mass matrix

messages.author: 3f37be0cf708d442
messages.subject: understanding number of elements in the mass matrix
parts:
Hello,

I fail to understand the number of entries in the
diagonal of the mass matrix of the following hierarchical 
regression model:

parameters {
  matrix[K,1] z;
  cholesky_factor_corr[K] L_Omega;
  real<lower=0, upper=pi()/2> tau_unif[K];    
  matrix[K,1] gamma;                            
  matrix[K,1] alpha;   

  real<lower=0, upper=pi()/2> phi_unif;
  }

transformed parameters {
  matrix[K,1] beta;
  vector<lower=0>[K] tau;
  real<lower=0> phi;
  for (k in 1:K) tau[k] <- 2.5 * tan(tau_unif[k]);
  beta <- gamma + (diag_pre_multiply(tau,L_Omega) * z);
  phi <- 5 * tan(phi_unif);
}

model {
  vector[N_train] thetas;
  vector[N_train] etas;

  // sample parameters
  // tau_unif ~ uniform(0, pi()/2); // not necessary
  to_vector(z) ~ normal(0,1);
  L_Omega ~ lkj_corr_cholesky(2);
  to_vector(gamma) ~ normal(0,2); # orig scale = 5
  
  alpha[K,1] ~ normal(0,5); # orig scale = 5
  alpha[1:(K-1),1] ~ normal(0,2); # orig scale = 5

  thetas <- to_vector(sx * to_matrix(alpha));
  etas <- to_vector(sx * beta);
  
  ...
}

When K is 26 and L is 1, I would have thought that the diagonal 
of the mass matrix should have 456 elements:
- 26 for z
- 351 for L_Omega
- 26 for gamma
- 26 for alpha
- 26 for taun_unif
- 1 for phi_unif

but I find only 430 elements. 

I must be understanding something incorrectly and would
be grateful for a hint ;-)

Guido

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] understanding number of elements in the mass matrix
parts:
The mass matrix corresponds to the unconstrained parameterization,
so L_Omega adds only K (K - 1) / 2 elements accounting for the 26
less elements that you see.

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] understanding number of elements in the mass matrix
parts:
This is good to remind people because when we tell them
to put things on the unit scale, we mean on the unconstrained
parameters. The chapter of the manual near the end on constraint
transforms has all the details.

- Bob
